questions.question: T: P₂ → P₂, T(p(x)) = p(x + 1). Ordered basis B = {1, x, x²} ke respect me `[T]_B` kya hai?
questions.explanation: T(1) = 1, coordinates (1, 0, 0). T(x) = x + 1, coordinates (1, 1, 0). T(x²) = (x + 1)² = 1 + 2x + x², coordinates (1, 2, 1). Inhe columns me likho: [[1, 1, 1], [0, 1, 2], [0, 0, 1]]. [[1, 0, 0], [1, 1, 0], [1, 2, 1]] transpose hai (coordinates rows me likh diye). [[1, 1, 1], [0, 1, 1], [0, 0, 1]] me (x + 1)² ke 2x ka coefficient 1 le liya, aur identity tab aati hai jab maan liya ki shift se koi coefficient nahi badalta.

questions.question: B = {(1, 1), (1, 0)} ek ordered basis hai aur `[T]_B` = [[1, 2], [0, −1]] (domain aur codomain dono me B). Standard coordinates me T(2, 1) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Step 1: (2, 1) = a(1, 1) + b(1, 0) se a = 1, b = 1, to `[v]_B` = (1, 1). Step 2: `[T(v)]_B` = [[1, 2], [0, −1]] × (1, 1) = (3, −1). Step 3: wapas standard me: T(v) = 3(1, 1) − 1·(1, 0) = (2, 3). (3, −1) B-coordinates hain, step 3 chhoot gaya. (4, −1) tab aata hai jab matrix ko seedha (2, 1) par laga diya (step 1 chhoot gaya), aur (3, 4) usi galat result ko B se wapas convert karne par aata hai.

questions.question: Ordered basis B = {b₁, b₂} ke respect me `[T]_B` = [[1, 2], [3, 4]] hai. Ab order badal kar B′ = {b₂, b₁} lo (domain aur codomain dono me). `[T]_B′` kya hai?
questions.explanation: `[T]_B` ke columns se: T(b₁) = 1·b₁ + 3·b₂ aur T(b₂) = 2·b₁ + 4·b₂. B′ me pehla vector b₂ hai: T(b₂) = 4·b₂ + 2·b₁, to B′-coordinates (4, 2), ye pehla column. T(b₁) = 3·b₂ + 1·b₁, coordinates (3, 1), doosra column. To [[4, 3], [2, 1]]: columns bhi swap aur rows bhi swap. [[2, 1], [4, 3]] me sirf columns swap kiye (domain ka order), codomain ka order bhool gaye. [[3, 4], [1, 2]] me sirf rows swap hui, aur [[1, 3], [2, 4]] sirf transpose hai.

questions.question: B = {(1, 0), (1, 1)} ordered basis hai (domain aur codomain dono me) aur `[T]_B` = [[2, 0], [0, 3]]. T ki standard matrix kya hai?
questions.explanation: `[T]_B` diagonal hai, to T(b₁) = 2b₁ = (2, 0) aur T(b₂) = 3b₂ = (3, 3). Standard matrix ke columns T(e₁) aur T(e₂) hote hain. e₁ = b₁, to T(e₁) = (2, 0). e₂ = b₂ − b₁, to T(e₂) = (3, 3) − (2, 0) = (1, 3). Standard matrix [[2, 1], [0, 3]]. Check: [[2, 1], [0, 3]]·(1, 1) = (3, 3) = 3b₂. [[2, 0], [0, 3]] wo trap hai jo maan leta hai ki basis badalne se matrix nahi badalti. [[2, 3], [0, 3]] me T(b₂) ko hi doosra column bana diya, jabki column T(e₂) hona chahiye. [[2, −1], [0, 3]] me conversion ulti direction me ho gaya (ye basis {(1, 0), (−1, 1)} ki matrix hai, jiske vectors e₁ aur e₂ ke B-coordinates hain); check se pakda jaata hai: [[2, −1], [0, 3]]·(1, 1) = (1, 3) ≠ 3b₂.

weeks.title: Inner products and Gram–Schmidt
weeks.summary: Inner product se length, angle aur orthogonality define karte hain, aur Gram–Schmidt process se kisi bhi basis ko orthonormal basis me badalna seekhte hain.
concepts: **Inner product** ⟨u, v⟩ ek number deta hai aur ye rules follow karta hai: symmetric (⟨u, v⟩ = ⟨v, u⟩), har argument me linear, aur positive (⟨v, v⟩ > 0 jab v ≠ 0). ℝⁿ me standard inner product dot product hai.
**Angle**: cos θ = ⟨u, v⟩ / (‖u‖ ‖v‖).
**Orthogonal**: ⟨u, v⟩ = 0. **Orthonormal set**: har pair orthogonal aur har vector ki length 1.
**Useful fact**: non-zero orthogonal vectors hamesha linearly independent hote hain.
**Projection**: v ka u par projection = (⟨v, u⟩ / ⟨u, u⟩) u. v minus ye projection, u ke perpendicular hota hai.
**Gram–Schmidt**: u₁ = v₁; u₂ = v₂ − proj of v₂ on u₁; u₃ = v₃ − (projections on u₁ aur u₂). Aakhir me har uᵢ ko uski length se divide karke orthonormal basis milta hai.

example.problem: v₁ = (1, 1, 0) aur v₂ = (1, 0, 1) par Gram–Schmidt lagao aur orthonormal set banao.
steps: Normalize: ‖u₁‖ = √2, to e₁ = (1/√2, 1/√2, 0). u₂ ko 2 se multiply karke (1, −1, 2) lo (direction same), ‖(1, −1, 2)‖ = √6, to e₂ = (1/√6, −1/√6, 2/√6).

mistakes: Projection me ⟨u, u⟩ se divide karna bhool jaana ya ‖u‖ (bina square) se divide karna. Formula me denominator ⟨u, u⟩ = ‖u‖² hai.
Gram–Schmidt me v₂ se projection subtract karne ki jagah add kar dena. Hamesha check karo ki ⟨u₁, u₂⟩ = 0 aa raha hai.
Non-standard inner product diya ho tab bhi normal dot product use kar lena. Question me diya gaya formula hi use karo.
revision: proj of v on u = (⟨v, u⟩ / ⟨u, u⟩) u
Gram–Schmidt: u₂ = v₂ − proj of v₂ on u₁, phir normalize

questions.question: Standard inner product me ‖(3, −4)‖ kitna hai?
questions.explanation: ‖v‖ = √(3² + (−4)²) = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5. 25 tab aata hai jab square root lena bhool gaye. 7 tab jab components ko seedha add kiya (|3| + |−4|).

questions.question: Standard dot product ke saath inme se kaunsa pair orthogonal hai?
questions.explanation: (2, 1, −1)·(1, −1, 1) = 2 − 1 − 1 = 0, isliye orthogonal. Baaki ke dot products: 1 + 2 + 3 = 6, 1 + 0 + 0 = 1, 1 − 1 + 1 = 1, koi bhi zero nahi.

questions.question: Standard inner product me v = (2, 3) ka u = (1, 1) par projection kya hai?
questions.explanation: ⟨v, u⟩ = 2 + 3 = 5, ⟨u, u⟩ = 1 + 1 = 2. Projection = (5/2)(1, 1) = (5/2, 5/2). (5, 5) tab aata hai jab ⟨u, u⟩ se divide karna bhool gaye. (5/√2, 5/√2) tab jab ‖u‖ se divide kiya, ‖u‖² se nahi.

questions.question: Vectors (1, 0, 1) aur (0, 1, 1) ke beech angle kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Dot product = 0 + 0 + 1 = 1. Dono ki length √2. cos θ = 1/(√2·√2) = 1/2, to θ = 60°. 90° tab aata hai jab koi maan le ki alag positions par zeros hain to perpendicular honge, par teesra component dono me 1 hai.

questions.question: v₁ = (1, 0) aur v₂ = (3, 2) par Gram–Schmidt lagaya. Normalize karne se pehle u₂ kya hoga?
questions.explanation: u₁ = (1, 0). Projection of v₂ on u₁ = (3/1)(1, 0) = (3, 0). u₂ = (3, 2) − (3, 0) = (0, 2). Check: (1, 0)·(0, 2) = 0. (3, 0) sirf projection hai, u₂ nahi. (6, 2) tab aata hai jab projection subtract ki jagah add kar diya.

questions.question: ℝ² par inner product ⟨u, v⟩ = 2u₁v₁ + u₂v₂ diya hai (u = (u₁, u₂), v = (v₁, v₂)). k ki kis value ke liye (1, k) aur (2, −4) is inner product me orthogonal hain?
questions.explanation: ⟨(1, k), (2, −4)⟩ = 2·1·2 + k·(−4) = 4 − 4k. Isko 0 rakho: k = 1. k = 1/2 trap hai: wo normal dot product (2 − 4k = 0) se aata hai, jabki question me weighted inner product diya hai.

questions.question: (1, 2, −2) ki direction me unit vector kya hai?
questions.explanation: ‖(1, 2, −2)‖ = √(1 + 4 + 4) = √9 = 3. Unit vector = v/‖v‖ = (1/3, 2/3, −2/3). (1/9, 2/9, −2/9) me ‖v‖² = 9 se divide kar diya. (1/5, 2/5, −2/5) me components ke absolute values ka sum 5 use kiya. (−1/3, −2/3, 2/3) bhi unit vector hai, par ulti direction me.

questions.question: Standard dot product ke saath inme se kaunsa set orthonormal hai?
questions.explanation: (3/5, 4/5)·(−4/5, 3/5) = −12/25 + 12/25 = 0, aur dono ki length √(9/25 + 16/25) = 1. To ye orthonormal hai. {(1, 1), (1, −1)} orthogonal hai par lengths √2 hain, 1 nahi. {(3/5, 4/5), (4/5, 3/5)} me dono unit vectors hain par dot product 24/25 ≠ 0. {(1, 0), (1/√2, 1/√2)} ka dot product 1/√2 ≠ 0.

questions.question: ⟨u, v⟩ = 3 aur ⟨u, w⟩ = −2 hai. ⟨u, 2v − w⟩ kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Inner product har argument me linear hai: ⟨u, 2v − w⟩ = 2⟨u, v⟩ − ⟨u, w⟩ = 2·3 − (−2) = 6 + 2 = 8. 4 tab aata hai jab −(−2) ko −2 le liya (6 − 2). 1 me 2 se multiply karna bhool gaye (3 − 2).

questions.question: ‖u‖ = 3, ‖v‖ = 4 aur ⟨u, v⟩ = 2 hai. ‖u + v‖² kitna hai?
questions.explanation: ‖u + v‖² = ⟨u + v, u + v⟩ = ‖u‖² + 2⟨u, v⟩ + ‖v‖² = 9 + 4 + 16 = 29. 25 tab aata hai jab u aur v ko orthogonal maan kar cross term chhod diya. 27 me cross term sirf ek baar gina, jabki ⟨u, v⟩ aur ⟨v, u⟩ dono aate hain. 49 = (3 + 4)², jo sirf tab hota jab u aur v ek hi direction me hon.

questions.question: v = (4, 2) aur u = (1, 1). v ka woh component kya hai jo u ke perpendicular hai (yaani v me se u par v ka projection ghatane par jo bachta hai)?
questions.explanation: Projection = (⟨v, u⟩/⟨u, u⟩)u = (6/2)(1, 1) = (3, 3). Perpendicular part = v − projection = (4, 2) − (3, 3) = (1, −1). Check: (1, −1)·(1, 1) = 0. (3, 3) sirf projection hai. (−2, −4) tab aata hai jab ⟨u, u⟩ se divide nahi kiya (v − 6u). (7, 5) me projection ghatane ki jagah jod diya.

questions.question: v₁ = (1, 1, 1), v₂ = (1, 2, 3), v₃ = (1, 0, 0) par Gram–Schmidt lagaya; u₁ = v₁ aur u₂ = (−1, 0, 1) mile. Normalize karne se pehle u₃ kya hoga?
questions.explanation: u₃ = v₃ − (⟨v₃, u₁⟩/⟨u₁, u₁⟩)u₁ − (⟨v₃, u₂⟩/⟨u₂, u₂⟩)u₂. Yahan ⟨v₃, u₁⟩ = 1, ⟨u₁, u₁⟩ = 3; ⟨v₃, u₂⟩ = −1, ⟨u₂, u₂⟩ = 2. To u₃ = (1, 0, 0) − (1/3)(1, 1, 1) + (1/2)(−1, 0, 1) = (1/6, −1/3, 1/6). Check: u₃·u₁ = 1/6 − 1/3 + 1/6 = 0 aur u₃·u₂ = −1/6 + 1/6 = 0. (2/3, −1/3, −1/3) me u₂ wala projection ghatana bhool gaye, aur (1/2, 0, 1/2) me u₁ wala. (7/6, −1/3, −5/6) me u₂ wale projection ka sign ulta lag gaya.

questions.question: ℝ² par inner product ⟨u, v⟩ = u₁v₁ + 2u₂v₂ hai. Is inner product me v₁ = (1, 1), v₂ = (1, 0) par Gram–Schmidt lagao. Normalize karne se pehle u₂ kya hai?
questions.explanation: u₁ = (1, 1). ⟨v₂, u₁⟩ = 1·1 + 2·0·1 = 1 aur ⟨u₁, u₁⟩ = 1 + 2·1 = 3. u₂ = (1, 0) − (1/3)(1, 1) = (2/3, −1/3). Check: ⟨u₁, u₂⟩ = 1·(2/3) + 2·1·(−1/3) = 0. (1/2, −1/2) normal dot product se aata hai (⟨u₁, u₁⟩ = 2 le liya); wo standard sense me orthogonal hai, par diye gaye inner product me ⟨u₁, u₂⟩ = 1/2 − 1 ≠ 0. (4/3, 1/3) me projection ghatane ki jagah jod diya.

questions.question: u₁ = (1, 1, 0), u₂ = (1, −1, 1), u₃ = (−1, 1, 2) aapas me orthogonal hain. Agar v = (3, 1, 4) = c₁u₁ + c₂u₂ + c₃u₃ ho, to c₃ kya hai?
questions.explanation: Orthogonal vectors ke saath har coefficient alag se nikalta hai: v ka u₃ ke saath inner product lo, baaki terms 0 ho jaate hain, to ⟨v, u₃⟩ = c₃⟨u₃, u₃⟩. ⟨v, u₃⟩ = −3 + 1 + 8 = 6 aur ⟨u₃, u₃⟩ = 1 + 1 + 4 = 6, to c₃ = 6/6 = 1. Isi tarah c₁ = 4/2 = 2 aur c₂ = 6/3 = 2; check: 2(1, 1, 0) + 2(1, −1, 1) + (−1, 1, 2) = (3, 1, 4). 6 tab aata hai jab ⟨u₃, u₃⟩ se divide nahi kiya, aur √6 jab ‖u₃‖ se divide kiya. 2 to c₁ (ya c₂) hai.

questions.question: ‖u‖ = 3, ‖v‖ = 2, aur u + v aur u − 2v orthogonal hain. ⟨u, v⟩ kitna hai?
questions.explanation: ⟨u + v, u − 2v⟩ = ⟨u, u⟩ − 2⟨u, v⟩ + ⟨v, u⟩ − 2⟨v, v⟩ = 9 − ⟨u, v⟩ − 8 = 1 − ⟨u, v⟩. Orthogonal hain, to ye 0 hai: ⟨u, v⟩ = 1. 1/3 tab aata hai jab cross terms ko −2⟨u, v⟩ − ⟨u, v⟩ = −3⟨u, v⟩ le liya (sign ki galti). −1 me aakhri step ka sign ulta hua, aur 17 tab aata hai jab −2⟨v, v⟩ ko +8 le liya (9 + 8).

weeks.title: Multivariable calculus basics
weeks.summary: Do variables ke functions ke partial derivatives, gradient aur directional derivative nikalna seekhte hain, aur Hessian se critical points ko classify karte hain.
concepts: **Partial derivative** ∂f/∂x: baaki variables ko constant maan kar sirf x ke respect me differentiate karo. Isi tarah ∂f/∂y.
**Gradient** ∇f = (∂f/∂x, ∂f/∂y). Ye ek vector hai jo function ke sabse tez badhne ki direction batata hai.
**Directional derivative**: unit vector u ki direction me rate of change `D_u f` = ∇f · u. Direction vector agar unit nahi hai to pehle uski length se divide karo.
**Maximum rate**: sabse zyada badhne ka rate ‖∇f‖ hota hai, aur wo ∇f ki direction me milta hai.
**Critical point**: jahan ∇f = 0, yaani ∂f/∂x = 0 aur ∂f/∂y = 0 dono.
**Hessian** H = [[∂²f/∂x², ∂²f/∂x∂y], [∂²f/∂y∂x, ∂²f/∂y²]]. Smooth functions me mixed partials equal hote hain.
**Second derivative test**: D = det(H) = `f_xx·f_yy − (f_xy)²`. D > 0 aur ∂²f/∂x² > 0 ⇒ local min; D > 0 aur ∂²f/∂x² < 0 ⇒ local max; D < 0 ⇒ saddle point; D = 0 ⇒ test inconclusive.

example.problem: f(x, y) = x² + xy + y² − 3x ke critical points nikalo aur classify karo.
steps: Dono ko 0 rakho. Doosri se x = −2y.
Pehli me rakho: 2(−2y) + y − 3 = 0, yaani −3y = 3, to y = −1 aur x = 2. Critical point (2, −1).
Answer: (2, −1) par local minimum hai, minimum value −3.

mistakes: Partial derivative lete waqt doosre variable wale terms ko bhi differentiate kar dena. ∂/∂x me y constant hai, to 2y² ka ∂/∂x zero hai.
Directional derivative me direction vector ko unit banana bhool jaana. (3, 4) ki jagah (3/5, 4/5) use karo.
Sirf ∂²f/∂x² > 0 dekh kar minimum bol dena. Pehle D ka sign dekho; D < 0 ho to saddle point hai.
revision: D = `f_xx·f_yy − (f_xy)²`: D > 0 min/max, D < 0 saddle, D = 0 inconclusive

questions.question: f(x, y) = x³y + 2y² ho, to ∂f/∂x kya hai?
questions.explanation: y ko constant maano. x³y ka ∂/∂x = 3x²y, aur 2y² me x nahi hai to uska ∂/∂x = 0. Answer 3x²y. 3x²y + 4y tab aata hai jab 2y² ko bhi differentiate kar diya. x³ + 4y ∂f/∂y hai.

questions.question: f(x, y) = x² + 3y ka gradient point (1, 2) par kya hai?
questions.explanation: ∂f/∂x = 2x = 2 (x = 1 par), ∂f/∂y = 3 (constant). ∇f(1, 2) = (2, 3). 7 function ki value f(1, 2) = 1 + 6 hai, gradient nahi; gradient hamesha vector hota hai.

questions.question: f(x, y) = x² + y² ka point (1, 2) par vector (3, 4) ki direction me directional derivative kya hai?
questions.explanation: ∇f = (2x, 2y) = (2, 4). Unit vector u = (3, 4)/5 = (3/5, 4/5). `D_u f` = 2·(3/5) + 4·(4/5) = 6/5 + 16/5 = 22/5. 22 tab aata hai jab (3, 4) ko unit banaye bina use kiya. 2√5 = ‖∇f‖, jo maximum rate hai, is direction ka rate nahi.

questions.question: f(x, y) = x²y³ ho, to ∂²f/∂x∂y (mixed partial) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Pehle ∂f/∂x = 2xy³. Phir y ke respect me: ∂/∂y (2xy³) = 6xy². Doosre order me bhi same aata hai: ∂f/∂y = 3x²y², phir ∂/∂x = 6xy². 2xy³ sirf pehla step hai, aur 3x²y² sirf ∂f/∂y.

questions.question: f(x, y) = 3x + 4y ka kisi bhi point par maximum rate of increase kitna hai?
questions.explanation: ∇f = (3, 4) har jagah. Maximum rate = ‖∇f‖ = √(9 + 16) = 5. 7 tab aata hai jab components seedhe add kar diye. 25 me square root lena bhool gaye.

questions.question: f(x, y) = x² − 4xy + y² ke critical point (0, 0) ki nature kya hai?
questions.explanation: ∂f/∂x = 2x − 4y, ∂f/∂y = −4x + 2y; dono zero sirf (0, 0) par. Hessian [[2, −4], [−4, 2]], D = 2·2 − (−4)² = 4 − 16 = −12 < 0, isliye saddle point. Check: f(1, 1) = 1 − 4 + 1 = −2 < 0 jabki f(1, 0) = 1 > 0. Sirf ∂²f/∂x² = 2 > 0 dekh kar minimum bolna trap hai.

questions.question: f(x, y) = 4x²y³ − 5xy + 7x ho, to ∂f/∂y kya hai?
questions.explanation: x ko constant maano. 4x²y³ ka ∂/∂y = 4x²·3y² = 12x²y², −5xy ka ∂/∂y = −5x, aur 7x me y nahi hai to uska ∂/∂y = 0. Answer 12x²y² − 5x. 8xy³ − 5y + 7 to ∂f/∂x hai. 12x²y² − 5x + 7 me 7x ko bhi differentiate karke 7 rakh diya, jabki y ke respect me wo constant hai. 12x²y² − 5xy me −5xy ko differentiate hi nahi kiya.

questions.question: f(x, y) = x² + y² − 4x + 6y ka critical point kya hai?
questions.explanation: ∂f/∂x = 2x − 4 = 0 se x = 2, aur ∂f/∂y = 2y + 6 = 0 se y = −3. Critical point (2, −3). (−2, 3) me dono signs ulte ho gaye. (4, −6) tab aata hai jab 2x − 4 = 0 aur 2y + 6 = 0 me 2 se divide karna bhool gaye. (0, 0) par ∇f = (−4, 6) ≠ 0.

questions.question: f(x, y) = 3x² + 4xy − y² ka Hessian kya hai?
questions.explanation: ∂f/∂x = 6x + 4y aur ∂f/∂y = 4x − 2y. Phir ∂²f/∂x² = 6, ∂²f/∂y² = −2, aur mixed partial ∂²f/∂x∂y = 4. Hessian [[6, 4], [4, −2]]. [[3, 2], [2, −1]] me sab entries aadhi kar di (wo Hessian nahi hai). [[6, 2], [2, −2]] me mixed partial ko 4/2 = 2 le liya. [[6, 4], [4, −1]] me −y² ko differentiate karte waqt 2 ka factor chhoot gaya.

questions.question: f(x, y) = x² + 3y². Point (1, 1) se kis direction me chalne par f sabse tez ghatta hai?
questions.explanation: ∇f = (2x, 6y), to (1, 1) par ∇f = (2, 6). Sabse tez badhna ∇f ki direction me hota hai, aur sabse tez ghatna −∇f = (−2, −6) ki direction me, jo (−1, −3) wali direction hi hai. (1, 3) to sabse tez badhne ki direction hai. (3, 1) aur (−3, −1) me gradient ke components ulte likh diye.

questions.question: f(x, y) = x² + 2xy + y² ka critical point (0, 0) hai. (0, 0) par second derivative test (D = `f_xx·f_yy − (f_xy)²` ke saath) kya verdict deta hai?
options: D > 0 aur ∂²f/∂x² > 0, to test local minimum batata hai
D < 0, to test saddle point batata hai
D > 0 aur ∂²f/∂x² < 0, to test local maximum batata hai
questions.explanation: ∂²f/∂x² = 2, ∂²f/∂y² = 2, ∂²f/∂x∂y = 2, to D = 2·2 − 2² = 0 aur test koi verdict nahi deta. Sawaal test ke conclusion ka hai, f ke behaviour ka nahi: f = (x + y)² ≥ 0 = f(0, 0), to (0, 0) asal me local minimum hai, par strict nahi, kyunki poori line y = −x par f = 0 hai. Us line ke along f flat hai, isi wajah se D = 0 aata hai aur test decide nahi kar paata; f ko seedha dekhna padta hai. Pehla option galat hai kyunki uska premise D > 0 hi galat hai; sirf ∂²f/∂x² = 2 > 0 dekh kar 'local minimum' bol dena trap hai.

questions.question: f(x, y) = x³ − 3x + y² ke critical points aur unki nature kya hai?
questions.explanation: ∂f/∂x = 3x² − 3 = 0 se x = ±1, aur ∂f/∂y = 2y = 0 se y = 0: points (1, 0) aur (−1, 0). ∂²f/∂x² = 6x, ∂²f/∂y² = 2, ∂²f/∂x∂y = 0, to D = 12x. (1, 0): D = 12 > 0 aur ∂²f/∂x² = 6 > 0, local minimum. (−1, 0): D = −12 < 0, saddle point. '(−1, 0) local maximum' wo trap hai jo sirf ∂²f/∂x² = −6 < 0 dekhta hai, D ka sign nahi.

questions.question: f(x, y) = x²y ka point (1, 2) par kis unit direction u me directional derivative `D_u f` = 0 hai?
questions.explanation: ∇f = (2xy, x²), to (1, 2) par ∇f = (4, 1). `D_u f` = ∇f · u = 0 ke liye u ko ∇f ke perpendicular hona chahiye: 4u₁ + u₂ = 0, jaise (1, −4)/√17. Check: 4·1 + 1·(−4) = 0. (4/√17, 1/√17) ∇f ki direction hai, jahan rate maximum (√17) hai, aur (−4/√17, −1/√17) minimum rate (−√17) ki direction hai. (1/√17, 4/√17) ke liye 4 + 4 = 8 ≠ 0.

questions.question: f(x, y) = x² + kxy + 4y². k ki kin values par critical point (0, 0) saddle point hai?
questions.explanation: ∂²f/∂x² = 2, ∂²f/∂y² = 8, ∂²f/∂x∂y = k. D = 2·8 − k² = 16 − k². Saddle ke liye D < 0: k² > 16, yaani |k| > 4 (k > 4 ya k < −4). 'k > 4' me negative values chhoot gayi (k = −5 par bhi D = −9 < 0). |k| < 4 par D > 0 aur ∂²f/∂x² > 0, to wahan local minimum hai. |k| > 2√2 tab aata hai jab 4y² ka second derivative 8 ki jagah 4 le liya (D = 8 − k²).

questions.question: f(x, y) = x²y − 2xy ke critical points ke baare me kya sahi hai?
options: 1 critical point (0, 0), jo saddle point hai
2 critical points; (0, 0) saddle aur (2, 0) local minimum
2 critical points (0, 0) aur (2, 0), dono saddle points
questions.explanation: ∂f/∂x = 2xy − 2y = 2y(x − 1) aur ∂f/∂y = x² − 2x = x(x − 2). Doosri se x = 0 ya x = 2; dono me x − 1 ≠ 0, to pehli se y = 0. Points (0, 0) aur (2, 0). (1, 0) par ∂f/∂y = −1 ≠ 0, to wo critical point nahi. ∂²f/∂x² = 2y, ∂²f/∂y² = 0, ∂²f/∂x∂y = 2x − 2. (0, 0): D = 0 − (−2)² = −4 < 0, saddle. (2, 0): D = 0 − 2² = −4 < 0, ye bhi saddle. Sirf ∂f/∂x = 0 se x = 1 le lena trap hai; dono partials ek saath zero hone chahiye.
